## Core Features Found in Business Process Management Software


Each tool offers something different, but these are the most common features you’ll see:


### Process Modeling


Process modeling is where you design how work should move before anyone touches a live request.


You open the builder, grab a *“Task”* block, drop it on the canvas, and connect it to the next step with an arrow. That simple action becomes your business process model.


However, since processes rarely move in a straight line, you can build *“If-Then”* logic directly into the model. You can also attach forms to steps, so for example, when the flow reaches *“Approve Invoice,”* the invoice appears with approve or reject buttons ready.


### Workflow Orchestration


The system monitors each request and pushes it forward based on the logic you defined earlier.


Let’s say Person A clicks *“Submit.”* The task then moves to Person B instantly, which helps teams manage workflows without chasing updates.


More advanced routing handles complex processes.


During onboarding, HR can submit a request that notifies IT to prepare equipment, finance to create payroll records, and facilities to assign a desk at the same time. The workflow waits until each step finishes before moving forward, which keeps your business operations organized.


### APIs and Integrations Capabilities


[Application programming interfaces (APIs)](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/10-top-api-integration-platforms-for-2025) and integration capabilities connect[BPM software](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/10-top-bpm-tools-for-enterprises) to other enterprise systems.


An API acts like an agreement between two programs. One system can request data, and the other responds immediately. Webhooks reverse that flow by sending data automatically when an event occurs, such as a payment confirmation that pushes a workflow to the next step.


Many platforms offer plug-and-play connectors for tools such as CRM, accounting, and project management systems. After login, the systems exchange information.


Seamless integration with other[enterprise systems](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/top-5-enterprise-automation-tools) improves operational efficiency and keeps process management connected to your daily business systems.


### Reporting and Analytics


As workflows run, reporting and analytics show how well they perform.


Dashboards display how many requests remain active, how long each step takes, and where delays appear.


Heat maps, on the other hand, reveal patterns that help identify bottlenecks. If contracts pause in *“Legal Review”* for four days on average, you know exactly where to adjust staffing or rules.


These reporting capabilities provide valuable insights that support continuous improvement. With concrete data to calculate and visualize key performance indicators (KPIs), you can track process efficiency over weeks and months.

### 2. Kissflow


Image Source: kissflow .


com


Kissflow, a workflow automation software, bridges the gap between business people who understand how work should flow and IT people who usually configure systems.


You start with a form. Then, build the digital document that collects the data, and add logic where needed. For example, you can hide the *“Car Model”* field unless the user selects *“Travel Type: Driving.”*


After the form, you define the steps, such as: *Initiation → Manager Approval → Finance Review.*


The builder uses a straightforward step-by-step layout. You decide who can see what at each stage. An employee may see the total amount, while only a manager sees the *“Risk Score”* field.


Once you hit publish, the process goes live. Your employees see a *“Start”* button on their dashboard, and managers see a *“Tasks to Approve”* list.


#### Key Features


- **Step-by-step workflow builder** - You map the flow in simple order, such as *“Submission → Approval → Finance Review”* without technical diagrams.
- **Smart form logic** - You add rules directly into forms, like hiding or showing fields based on user input.
- **Role-based visibility** - You control who can view or edit specific data at each stage.
- **Parallel task execution** - It can trigger multiple tasks simultaneously, such as notifying IT, HR, and facilities during onboarding.
- **Cloud access** - The system runs in the browser and provides the flexibility to access and manage workflows from anywhere because it’s cloud-based.
- **Process monitoring** - You can monitor metrics like cycle time and throughput through live dashboards.
- **Integration support** - It connects to Slack, Salesforce, and Google Workspace to reduce manual updates.


#### Pricing


Kissflow offers the Basic plan starting at $2,500 per month, which includes unlimited workflows. Yet, it limits integrations, reporting depth, and external portals.


Larger organizations can move to the Enterprise plan with custom pricing.


### 3. Nintex


Image Source: nintex .


com


Nintex is often used for mapping and documenting processes before you automate anything. You start by capturing how work happens today, then improve it step by step to streamline operations.


It follows a[“low-code/no-code” philosophy](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/no-code-automation-tools) , so you don’t write scripts to[build workflows](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/how-to-build-ai-workflows-with-activepieces) . Instead, you open a visual designer and draw your business logic directly on the screen.


You place *“Action”* tiles, such as assign a task, send an email, or update a SharePoint list, onto a canvas and connect them in order. After defining the path, you link the workflow to your CRM or ERP, so data flows automatically between systems.


When older software doesn’t provide modern integrations, Nintex uses bots to handle repetitive manual tasks in old software with no API.


#### Key Features


- **Process mapping and documentation** - Used for mapping and documenting processes so you understand how work currently operates before automation begins.
- **AI process capture** - Uses AI to record user actions such as clicks and keystrokes on desktops to automatically generate accurate process maps.
- **Low-code workflow designer** - You drag and connect action tiles to build approvals, routing logic, and multi-step workflows without writing code.
- [Robotic process automation (RPA)](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/business-process-automation-vs-rpa) - Integrate robotic process automation to handle legacy applications that lack APIs.
- **Automated document generation** - Automatically creates professional Word, Excel, or PDF documents, such as contracts or invoices, directly from your data.
- **Enterprise monitoring** - Track workflow activity and identify delays as volume grows.


#### Pricing


Nintex does not list fixed pricing on its website.


### 4. Microsoft Power Automate


Image Source: microsoft .


com


[Microsoft Power Automate](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/microsoft-power-automate-alternative) lets you automate repetitive tasks and improve efficiency through a very simple logic: *Trigger → Action.*


When something happens, the system reacts. For example, when a file is uploaded to SharePoint, it can send an approval request through Teams immediately.


You can start from a template or build one from scratch. The drag-and-drop builder lets you add conditions without writing code. You can set a rule like *“IF the invoice is over $1,000, send to the CEO. IF NOT, auto-approve.”*


As of now, Power Automate offers connectors, which act as bridges to other apps, including Salesforce, Dropbox, and Slack. If older software lacks a modern connector or API, it uses bots to mimic human clicks and typing.


With AI features, it can read invoices, analyze email sentiment, or recognize data in images to route tasks properly. That combination helps automate repetitive tasks and improve efficiency in daily business operations.


#### Key Features


- **Trigger and action logic** - Build flows using a simple event-to-response structure that removes manual steps.
- **Template library** - Start from pre-built workflows or create custom flows for your needs.
- **Extensive connector network** - Connect with over 1,000 apps, including Microsoft services, Salesforce, Dropbox, and Slack.
- **Robotic process automation** - Use bots to interact with legacy systems that lack APIs.
- **Run history dashboard** - Monitor execution logs and track failed steps quickly.
- **Application support for business users** - Empowers business users and citizen developers to build applications quickly and conveniently.


#### Pricing


Microsoft offers the Premium plan that costs $15 per user per month and includes cloud flows, desktop flows, and process mining. The Process plan costs $150 per bot per month for unattended automation.


For $215 per bot per month, the Hosted Process plan includes a Microsoft-hosted virtual machine.


### 5. Appian


Image Source: appian .


com


Appian targets organizations that manage large, regulated business operations such as loan approvals, insurance claims, or government case handling.


It uses a *“Model-Driven”* architecture. You design a visual process model, and Appian instantly turns that drawing into a secure application that runs on web and mobile.


You can start by uploading your system logs. Appian’s process mining feature sees how your employees actually work and emphasizes where you’re losing money.


In the process modeler, you drag and drop *“Smart Services”* such as send email, write to database, or AI skill onto a canvas. It also uses built-in AI for intelligent document processing, automating routine tasks and managing complex operations more accurately.


#### Key Features


- **Model-driven architecture** - Design a visual process and deploy it instantly as a secure web and mobile application.
- **Process mining** - Upload logs so the system can analyze activity and highlight process inefficiencies.
- **Data fabric layer** - Connect enterprise systems without copying data, which eliminates manual data entry.
- **Enterprise case management** - Support dynamic case handling for complex operations that require flexible routing.
- **Performance dashboards** - Provide real-time insights to monitor process performance and adjust quickly.


#### Pricing


Appian doesn’t publish fixed pricing on its website.


### 6. ProcessMaker


Image Source: processmaker .


com


ProcessMaker uses a high-performance business process model and notation (BPMN) 2.0. It can follow international standards for how a process should look and act.


Through the Visual Process Modeler, you can drag and drop tasks, gateways (decision points), and events (triggers) onto a blank screen. Since it uses universal symbols such as events, gateways, and tasks, both business analysts and IT teams understand the same blueprint.


Aside from that, its newer Agentic AI features allow you to describe a process in English, and the system automatically drafts the workflow, forms, and backend logic.


Once published, the process appears in a workflow portal for users, which supports task management.


#### Key Features


- **Agentic AI builder** - Draft workflows automatically from English descriptions to speed up design.
- **Visual process modeler** - Drag tasks, gateways, and triggers onto a canvas to build structured flows.
- **Case and exception management** - It can manage cases where a human expert needs to handle exceptions that don’t follow a fixed path.
- **SLA reporting and analytics** - Managers can use service-level agreement (SLA) reports to see exactly who dropped the ball and where delays impact performance.
- **Enterprise integrations** - Connect CRM, enterprise resource planning (ERP), and document tools through APIs to unify systems.
- **Operational monitoring** - Dashboards support ongoing process optimization and oversight.


#### Pricing


ProcessMaker offers the Standard plan starting at around $3,000 per month. It includes unlimited processes and users, governance tools, and both development and production environments.


Organizations that need expanded capabilities can request the Professional or Enterprise pricing based on deployment size and feature requirements.


### 7. Bizagi


Image Source: bizagi .


com


Bizagi is an integrated BPM suite that allows organizations to model, automate processes, and manage them on a single platform. It is split into three core products: *Bizagi Modeler, Bizagi Studio, and Bizagi Automation.*


Bizagi follows a *“Data-First”* logic. While other tools focus on the arrows, Bizagi asks you to define the data model first. You identify objects such as *“Customer,” “Invoice,”* or *“Order.”*


Once the system understands your data, it automatically knows how to handle it throughout the workflow. The modeling environment makes it easy for anyone to begin diagramming their processes using common business process model standards, even if they are new to BPM.


It also centralizes your company’s policies so you can change a rule once and have it instantly update across every process in the company.


Before you go live, you can run simulations to see how your process performs under pressure and optimize workflows in advance.


#### Key Features


- **Lifecycle-based platform** - Move from modeling to deployment within one connected environment.
- **Data-first architecture** - Define business objects first so the system manages relationships automatically.
- **Centralized business rules engine** - Change a policy once and apply it instantly across every workflow.
- **Process simulation** - Test heavy volumes before launch to identify where queues will form.
- **Case management support** - It can handle cases where a human expert needs to jump between steps or add ad-hoc tasks in real time.
- **Integration layer** - Connect CRM, ERP, and legacy systems to keep data synchronized.
- **Performance dashboards** - Monitor active cases and workload to refine execution.


#### Pricing


Bizagi doesn’t publish pricing publicly.


### 8. FlowWright


Image Source: flowwright .


com


FlowWright is a low-code platform focused on serious business process automation.


Many tools separate *“drawing”* from *“doing.”* In FlowWright, the visual model is the logic that the engine executes. When you design a workflow on the screen, that diagram becomes the running system that streamlines processes in your business.


You open the graphical designer and map out tasks, approvals, and decision points. Compared to other platforms that separate the visual map from the technical code, FlowWright’s graphical process designer generates the actual logic that the engine runs.


When you want a faster starting point, you can describe a business process in simple language, and the[AI Copilot](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/ask-ai-code) will automatically draft the workflow, logic, and forms.


It even includes an out-of-the-box enterprise service bus (ESB) for handling event-based processing, which allows it to orchestrate work across multiple systems.


#### Key Features


- **Unified model and execution engine** - The workflow you design visually becomes the exact logic the system runs in production.
- **AI Copilot drafting** - Describe a process in simple language and generate workflows, forms, and routing rules automatically.
- **Enterprise service bus** - Built-in ESB support for event-driven processing between multiple applications.
- **Graphical rules designer** - Configure advanced decision logic to support business process automation without heavy coding.
- **Integration framework** - Connect CRM, ERP, and legacy systems to centralize automation capabilities.
- **Governance and versioncontrol** - Maintain detailed logs for compliance and accountability.


#### Pricing


FlowWright doesn’t publish pricing publicly.
